Boston, Mass. It must, however, be recognized that technological advances engender an element of elasticity with respect to the meaning of "adjacent." As transportation and communication networks improve, distances shrink. A determination of those areas which meet the "adjacent to" requirement must be made in light of modern transportation networks connecting the base municipality and outlying suburban areas.
The second commercial zone requirement - that the included suburban area be "commercially a part" of the base municipality - refers to the degree of economic interaction between these two areas. Various factors can be considered as indicia of interaction, including: (1) demographic trends relating to population movements between the city and outlying areas; (2) business migration from base municipality to suburbs; (3) the extent and nature of business or commercial dealings between city and suburbs; (4) mutuality of utilities and social services; (5) twoway traffic in employees, goods, and services; (6) whether suburban residents look to the base municipality for their cultural, social, recreational, educational, and medical needs; (7) wholesale and retail sales area for city business enterprises; (8) existence of branch stores in suburbs; and (9) area served by local communications and advertising media - newspapers, television, and radio.
